text:
Happy Sunday, and welcome to the early sunsets. With the clocks back, the sun drops at 4:41, and it'll set under a clear sky with temperatures still in the mid 50s. After that it cools off gently. Tonight is partly cloudy with a low around 45, so a light jacket is plenty for an evening walk and there's no frost to worry about.

Monday is the warmer day. Expect mostly sunny skies and a high near 64, with the models running anywhere from the low 60s to the upper 60s. The south breeze picks up a little but nothing you'll fight. Clouds build Monday night and the low holds near 47.

Tuesday is the one to watch. It turns cloudier, and light rain is possible in the afternoon and evening, though the models disagree on where it sets up. I'd bet on a few sprinkles at most, around a hundredth or two of rain. Monday is your best day to be outside.

  1. Temperatures increase this week, and there is the potential for some rain showers Tuesday and Tuesday night.
  2. A late week cold front will bring several days of rain
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 124 PM EST Sunday... Confidence has increased slightly in light rain showers Tuesday and Tuesday night. Confidence also continues to increase in warm temperatures on Wednesday, and highs across the St. Lawrence Valley of New York are expected to reach or surpass daily records.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: High 1034 mb pressure centered over the Northeast this afternoon will shift southeastward over to the mid Atlantic coast, drifting offshore over the next few days. This will turn flow more southerly to southwesterly across northern New York and Vermont, resulting in above average temperatures this week. Highs Monday and Tuesday afternoons will be widespread 60s. Lows fall only into the 40s tonight and Monday night. A tilted mid to upper level ridge will be positioned to our west through about Tuesday, moving eastwards this week. Depending on the positioning of an upper level vort max and surface boundaries, there could be just enough forcing and lift to produce some clouds and light rain, mainly along the international border and on high terrain on Tuesday and Tuesday night. The odd rain shower is possible Monday night in the Northeast Kingdom, but generally best convergence is north of the border at this time. Deterministic model solutions continue to vary widely on the position of these features, so uncertainty remains relatively high, even on Tuesday and Tuesday night. Highest chance of some measurable precipitation looks to be Tuesday afternoon and evening with 35-55% chance of rain for about the northern half of the forecast area, lower chances south. Regardless, temperatures continue to look warm for this time of year heading into mid and late week with highs likely reaching the upper 60s and lower 70s by Wednesday afternoon as southerly to southwesterly winds advect in even more warmth and 925 mb level temps climb to 11-16 C. Lows are expected to fall into the mid 40s to mid 50s Tuesday and Wednesday nights. KEY MESSAGE 2: Confidence continues to increase that a relatively strong low pressure and associated cold front will sweep through northern New York and Vermont by the end of the week. A closed low will be over the Upper Great Lakes by Wednesday. While timing is still a bit uncertain, we should see channeled flow keeping winds over Lake Champlain gusting to near 30mph on Thursday with rain overtaking the CWA on Friday ahead of the low. As the cold front sweeps through, we'll see high temperatures drop from the upper 60s Thursday down to the upper 40s by Saturday. A number of model solutions have the system interacting with another low off the Atlantic Seaboard, causing the low to partially cutoff from the main flow and allowing a slight chance of rain to persist through next Sunday.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Hopefully you’ve remembered to turn your clocks back 1 hour, as we’re back to Standard Time. After a chilly but fair Halloween, today will be mostly sunny and pleasantly warmer with highs in the 50s to around 60 degrees...not a bad way to start November and the second half of fall. Monday will be dry and even warmer with highs in the mid-50s to low 60s. The week will continue to be dry before the chance for rain increases late in the week. Election Day may have an isolated shower north, otherwise it will be mostly cloudy with highs in the 50s, though a few low 60s are possible. The warmest day will be Wednesday with plenty of sunshine and highs in the 60s. A few spots may even hit 70 degrees. It will be breezy, so we’ll have to keep an eye on the fire danger. The risk is currently high in parts of the region, but it’s not expected to reach red flag status. We’ll keep an eye on it. A storm system will bring some needed rain late in the week and possibly into next weekend, though models differ with the track and duration. As of now, Thursday is expected to be mostly cloudy with showers likely. Friday and Saturday are a bit more uncertain, but the chance for showers may continue. High temperatures those days will be in the 50s with lows in the 40s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-01T14:38:00Z — same caveat): Sunny and warmer Sunday, as a south breeze develops — Sunday turns milder, with highs in the 50s to near 60, as a light south breeze develops. High pressure brings a mostly sunny sky through the day. A few more clouds arrive tonight, with the risk for a spot shower late. It won't be as cold, with lows in the 30s and 40s. Most of the upcoming workweek looks mild for early November, with highs in the 60s for several days. Monday will feature a blend of sun and clouds. The warmup continues, thanks to an active south breeze. Highs reach the mid-60s. Tuesday looks mostly cloudy with a period of light rain possible, especially during the afternoon and evening, as a warm front lifts through. Highs fall back to the upper 50s. Wednesday looks to be the warmest day, as highs reach the low to mid-70s for many towns! Expect a partly sunny sky. An area of low pressure brings the chance for widespread, beneficial rain late week. A few showers are possible Thursday, especially by afternoon, as highs stay in the 60s. Rain may be steady at times on Friday, with highs falling back to the upper 50s.
